sources.title: Darul Ifta Birmingham: What is meant by flowing blood
sources.supports: The Hanafi rule distinguishes flowing blood or pus, including discharge absorbed before it can flow, from non-flowing traces.

sources.title: Dar al-Ifta: Ruling on blood from the nose
sources.supports: The source attributes non-nullification of nosebleeds to Malikis and Shafi‘is and distinguishes small amounts in the Hanbali position.

sources.title: Dar al-Ifta: Bleeding and ablution
sources.supports: Dar al-Ifta adopts non-nullification for wounds and nosebleeds and recommends renewal because of disagreement.

sources.title: Darul Ifta Birmingham: Bleeding gums during wudu
sources.supports: The answer distinguishes blood-dominant saliva from saliva-dominant mixtures in the ruling it presents.

review.notes: Reviewed all four named source pages. Hanafi flow/pus and gum rules remain attributed; Hanbali threshold is not quantified without support. Menstrual and continuous bleeding are outside this brief. Medical treatment instructions and invented hadith are absent. Questions from the combined research brief are covered on one canonical page. No app CTA for Islamful.
